title: Preserve the unique merge child's allocation when its content is corrected
consequence: When replaying the same explicit merge decision with exactly one persisted child, matching without child_keys still requires unchanged child value. A correction to that single child's definition produces a gap and retires its active identity, although the stable decision receipt, parent set, operation, scope and child kind identify that one child unambiguously. This prevents ordinary revision/correction while retaining the persisted explicit lineage decision.
reproducer: Reconcile North/South anonymous terms, explicitly merge their IDs into one Together term with decision_id merge-1, then replay exactly that decision while changing only Together.definition. The unchanged replay preserves review:e0000003; the corrected replay yields no assigned term ID and an active gap.

evidence.observed: ids(corrected) is {}, expected Together -> the existing merge child ID

expected_result_justification: The same explicit merge receipt has exactly one child in a known kind/scope. Its unique persisted allocation supplies identity evidence independently of text content; the task requires unambiguous correction and persisted lineage/replay. Stable child keys remain necessary for indistinguishable multiple children, but a one-child decision is already unambiguous.
required_change: Match an existing uniquely identified lineage child by its persisted receipt/decision and exact child contract independently of corrected content. Preserve gaps for genuine multi-child ambiguity or conflicting decisions; do not allocate a replacement or require unrelated semantic acceptance for a text correction.
required_verification: Keep the strict unique-child correction probe unchanged and make it retain the existing child ID/origin_key
Cover repeated correction and rename of a single merged child, retained old origins and exact historical parent references
Retain keyed identical split children, multiple-child ambiguity, changed/colliding decision rejection and unchanged replay tests
Re-run affected suites, full private canonical reproducibility and required checks
